messages:
sara-support: Heads up — enterprise customer reported flaky CI builds after we mirrored their private dependency. Repro steps + logs below. Seen this pattern before with replace/pseudo-version mismatches? @alex @jordan

alex: Can you paste the go.mod and the exact `go build` error?

sara-support: ```
module github.com/customer/app

require (
    github.com/redwood/inference-go v1.3.0
)

replace github.com/redwood/inference-go => github.com/redwood/inference-go v0.0.0-20250202020202-abcdefabcd
```

sara-support: Logs when running `go build` in CI:
```
$ go build ./...
go: github.com/redwood/inference-go@v0.0.0-20250202020202-abcdefabcd: parsing go.mod: module declares its path as: github.com/redwood/inference-go/v2
	but was required as: github.com/redwood/inference-go
```

alex: :eyes: That looks like a missing `/v2` module path. The replace pseudo-version points at a commit whose module path is v2, but the project requiring it is still using the v1 import path — so the tool is getting confused and falling back to pseudo-versions.

jordan-eng: If their code expects the v1 path but upstream migrated to v2, the go toolchain can generate pseudo-versions and cause semver/downgrade noise. Ask for `go env`, `go version`, and `GOPROXY` from the customer.

sara-support: env: `go version go1.20 linux/amd64`, `GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org,direct`. CI uses a private goproxy cache in front of the public proxy.

mike: Quick workaround: remove the `replace` and update the require/imports to use `github.com/redwood/inference-go/v2 v2.0.1` (update imports to `/v2`). Pin the exact release. Avoid publishing modules where a tag's major version doesn't match the module path.

jordan-eng: We should validate whether the tagged release actually contains `module .../v2` in its go.mod. If someone tagged v2 without updating the module path, that'll break consumers. @alex can you run `go list -m -json` against the tagged release or the pseudo-version?

alex: Tried `go list -m -json github.com/redwood/inference-go@v2.0.1` from a repro env — got checksum/404 errors from the private proxy. Looks like the private proxy cache served a pseudo-version earlier and the CI is stuck on that. Pinging infra to flush the proxy cache for that module.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Proxy cache invalidation job queued (job id: proxy-clear-4242).

sara-support: Customer accepted temporary workaround of switching to `/v2` require and removing replace. They want a permanent fix since their CI kept retrying (billing/timeouts).

alex: Escalating to eng-runtime: we should detect module path vs tag-major mismatch and surface a clearer error to customers rather than letting them loop on pseudo-versions. Also we should add a release-time check to prevent tagging without updating module path. I'll attach the logs.

jordan-eng: On it — I'll open an internal ticket with repro steps and suggest two fixes: 1) add a CI gate on release that validates `go.mod` module path matches the major in the git tag, 2) add a diagnostic in our SDK docs about not publishing replace directives for released modules.

sara-support: Copying the steps we gave the customer for the support doc: 1) remove `replace` directives that point to pseudo-versions, 2) update imports and `require` to use `/v2` and pin the tagged release, 3) run `go clean -modcache && go get github.com/redwood/inference-go/v2@v2.0.1`, 4) if behind a private proxy, flush the proxy cache.

alex: :thumbsup: I'll attach the CI logs to the ticket and follow up. Closing this thread once eng ticket is created.
